page: Google Cloud Platform e2-micro is a shared-core virtual machine belonging to the e2 server family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 vCPUs, which are mapped to a single physical core with hyper-threading enabled. However, CPU resources are shared, allocating only 1/8 of a physical core. The system is equipped with 1.0 GB of system memory, yielding 0.5 GB of RAM per vCPU, and contains no local storage or GPUs.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the bottom 10% across all tested categories. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests yielded scores of 132.9 and 171.0, respectively. Memory bandwidth is highly constrained, with read-only small block cached bandwidth measured at 9.73 GB/sec, dropping to 0.1 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Passmark CPU and memory scores are similarly low, at 201.56 and 176.45. Static web serving throughput is limited to 0.17 GB/sec.

This server type represents a highly cost-efficient tier designed for low-demand utility workloads. The primary tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation and minimal memory capacity, which severely limits throughput and processing speed. It is best suited for lightweight background tasks, basic automation scripts, low-traffic static web serving, or simple development and testing environments that do not require sustained compute or memory resources.
